speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, specifically regarding its color, shape, and distribution? Also, how long has the rash been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice a "slapped cheek" appearance on her face, and are the spots on her trunk and extremities lacy or net-like in pattern? I would also like to check if she has any swollen lymph nodes or joint pain.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, along with mild prodromal symptoms, is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
